input.content: Pattern: "Simplification" that removes an ownership/identity guard before a delete can clobber a newer record. In cleanup_setup (cleanup.py), the guard `if association and association["setup_id"] == setup_id: store.active.pop(workspace_id)` was collapsed to an unconditional `store.active.pop(workspace_id)`. Because another setup can complete and take over the workspace's single active slot before a failed setup's queued cleanup runs (documented in README), the unconditional pop evicts the live association owned by a DIFFERENT setup_id, so active_connection() returns None for a workspace that actually has a completed setup. Lesson: a guarded/conditional delete keyed on an ownership field is a correctness invariant ("remove only the association it owns"), not redundant verbosity — do not drop it during cleanup/simplification. Existing tests that only clean up a setup's own association pass for both versions and do not catch this; the discriminating test needs a second setup completing before the stale cleanup.
